script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JANE (mid-30s, warm smile), a homemaker, is making breakfast for her husband ROB (early 40s, stressed). They share a comfortable silence.

JANE
(laughs softly)
You know, when we were dating, you used to be so patient. Now you're always in a hurry.

ROB
(sighs)
Work's been crazy, Janey. I promise I'll make it up to you.

They share a look, and the tension in Rob's face begins to ease.

INT. LIVING ROOM - LATER

The children, MIKE (10), LIZ (8), and SAM (6), sit on the couch, each engrossed in their own devices.

JANE
(announcing)
Kids, time to get ready for school!

Mike groans and Liz pouts, but they both reluctantly get up. Sam, however, stays glued to his tablet.

INT. SAM'S BEDROOM - LATER

Janet enters the room, finding Sam still playing on his tablet.

JANE
(firm but gentle)
Sam, you need to get ready for school.

SAM
(whining)
But Mom, I'm almost done!

Janet sighs and sits down beside him.

JANE
You know what, Sammy? I used to feel the same way when I had to do things I didn't want to do. But sometimes, doing the right thing isn't always easy or fun. It's about making a commitment and following through with it.

They share a moment of understanding before Sam finally gets up and begins to get ready.

EXT. SCHOOL - DAY

Rob drops the kids off at school, then heads to work. Jane stays behind, gathering groceries for the week.

INT. SUPERMARKET - AFTERNOON

As Jane shops, she runs into her old friend PETER (late 30s), who seems troubled.

PETER
(hesitant)
Jane, it's been a long time. I need to talk to you about something.

JANE
(surprised)
Of course, Peter. What's on your mind?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LATER

They sit down at a table, and Peter opens up about his struggles with addiction. Jane listens attentively, her expression sympathetic.

PETER
(tearing up)
I've lost everything, Jane. My family, my friends, my job. I'm at rock bottom, and I don't know if I can climb back up.

JANE
(gently)
Peter, you can. You just need to take it one day at a time. And you're not alone. I'll be here for you, every step of the way.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Rob comes home from work, exhausted. Jane greets him with a warm smile and a hot meal.

JANE
(smiling)
Welcome home, dear. I made your favorite. How was your day?

ROB
(sighs)
Long and grueling. But seeing your face and hearing your voice makes it all worth it.

INT. KITCHEN - LATER

As they clean up the dishes, Rob confesses his fear of losing his job and the burden it puts on their family. Jane assures him that they will get through it together and that she believes in him.

EXT. PARK - NIGHT

Jane meets with Peter, who has managed to find a support group and is making progress in his recovery. They share a heartfelt moment, acknowledging the importance of forgiveness and the power of friendship.

FADE OUT.

THE END
